properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWS RSA signature suite (RS256/RS384/RS512 PKCS#1 v1.5 + PS256/PS384/PS512 PSS) exported by this JWT key-management library. Live chain: Algorithm.Create factory (Jwa/Algorithm.cs:36-42) → JwtOptions.Jws default (JwtOptions.cs:7 → Algorithm.cs:137, PS256) → SigningCredentials (Jwt/JwtService.cs:80) → Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens 8.23.0 signs with the RSA-3072 key from CryptoService.CreateRsaSecurityKey. Shor-vulnerable; deadline-class risk; ML-DSA-65.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-256/384/512 JWS signing constants. Live: Algorithm.Create selects HS256 as the HMAC default (Algorithm.cs:132 → JwtOptions.Jws if configured) and CryptoService.CreateHmacSecurityKey (CryptoService.cs:72-74) generates 64/128-byte CSPRNG keys via RandomNumberGenerator. Shared-secret property: any party able to verify can also mint. Practically quantum-resistant (Grover square-root only) — no PQ migration needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live RSA key generation at the heart of this JWT key-management library: CryptoService.CreateRsaSecurityKey calls RSA.Create(keySize) with keySize defaulting to 3072 bits (resolved from the method signature at CryptoService.cs:14) — adequate against classical attack, still Shor-vulnerable. KeyMaterial.GenerateRsa invokes it with the default. The same generated key serves JWS signing (RS256/PS256, covered by the JWT RS256/PS256 object) and JWE key transport (RSA-OAEP/RSA1_5) depending on the Algo

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWE key-transport constant "RSA-OAEP". Note: per RFC 7518 §4.3 this is RSAES-OAEP with SHA-1 hash and MGF1(SHA-1) — the library offers no RSA-OAEP-256 variant, so the default JWE key transport pairs a 3072-bit RSA key with SHA-1-based OAEP. Accepted as Encryption/RSA by the Algorithm factory (Algorithm.cs:17) and selected as the default JWE alg (Algorithm.cs:138 → JwtOptions.Jwe). Quantum: harvestable key transport (Shor) → ML-KEM-768, which requires a KEM/DEM redesign of the call, not a paramet

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA is a first-class supported JWS signature family in this library: the AlgorithmType.ECDsa switch arm in KeyMaterial dispatches to GenerateECDsa → CryptoService.CreateECDsaSecurityKey → ECDsa.Create(GetNamedECCurve(curve)) — a live keygen chain on NIST curves. The library's recommended/default JWS for the ECDsa type is ES256 on P-256 (Algorithm.cs:131). The 7 test sites (xUnit InlineData rows plus one key-creation test) exercise the same production paths; the shipped asset is the 8 src/ site

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA JWS constants ES256/ES384/ES512 mapping to P-256/P-384/P-521 (CryptoService.GetCurveType/GetNamedECCurve, ECDsa.Create(nistP*)). Default for AlgorithmType.ECDsa JWS is ES256 with P-256 (Algorithm.cs:136). Shor-vulnerable signature; ML-DSA-65.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live curve mapping in CryptoService.GetNamedECCurve: maps the JWK/RFC 7518 curve id "P-256" to .NET ECCurve.NamedCurves.nistP256. Called from CreateECDsaSecurityKey when generating ES256 keys (the library's recommended ECDSA JWS). Curve selection directive, decided by the alg name via GetCurveType (EcdsaSha256 → P256). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live curve selection for ES384/ES512 keys: GetCurveType maps EcdsaSha384→P-384 and EcdsaSha512→P-521 (CryptoService.cs:51-52), and GetNamedECCurve maps those JWK curve ids to nistP384/nistP521 (114-116). The "P512" arm is a deliberate alias for nistP521 — code comment: "treat 512 as 521. It was a bug in .NET Release." P-384 meets interim CNSA strength but remains Shor-vulnerable like all classical curves. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-2 family across the library: HS256/384/512 JWS constants + key generation (CryptoService.cs:72-74, HMACSHA256/384/512 with 64/128-byte CSPRNG keys) + the MAC halves of the A128/A192/A256CBC-HS* composite AEADs (including Aes192CbcHmacSha384, whose AES-CBC half is not otherwise inventoried) + test fixtures exercising all of them. Quantum-resistant in practice (Grover square-root); the key-distribution property (verifier = minter) is the real limitation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 family: A128KW key wrap + A128CBC-HS256 / A128GCM content encryption. Live: AES key generation at 128 bits (CryptoService.cs:88-93, Aes.Create), accepted in Algorithm factory (Algorithm.cs:11, 86-87) and the default JWE content encryption A128CBC-HS256 (Algorithm.cs:138-139). Grover halves 128→64-bit margin; below CNSA 2.0's 256-bit symmetric target — prefer A256GCM where policy requires it. All 49 sites genuine (constants, factory cases, keygen, tests).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM is a supported JWE content-encryption family: the JWA identifiers "A128GCM"/"A256GCM" are declared in EncryptionAlgorithmContent.cs:21/23 and whitelisted in Algorithm.WithContentEncryption (Algorithm.cs:87/91); the actual GCM encryption executes inside Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens when the JWE token is produced (the README notes .NET did not support RSA-OAEP with A128GCM, so the default content encryption is A128CBC-HS256 — AES-GCM is opt-in). Symmetric, so not harvest-now-decrypt-late

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live AES key generation in CryptoService.CreateAESSecurityKey: Aes.Create() with KeySize then set from the requested JWE key-management algorithm — Aes128KW→128, Aes256KW→256 — and GenerateKey() called (CryptoService.cs:88-92). These AES keys wrap the JWE content-encryption key (RFC 3394 key wrap executed by Microsoft.IdentityModel). The object's "AES-128 floor" grading is accurate: A128KW yields a 128-bit key; A256KW yields 256. Symmetric AE, not quantum-vulnerable in the Shor sense. Changeable

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 in DatabaseJsonWebKeyStore.DeterministicId: hashes "use:kty:previousId" into a GUID used as the database primary key for stored JWKs, so concurrent replicas insert one row instead of multiplying keys. Real SHA-256 in the shipped store assembly, but a non-security-purpose use (row identity, not integrity or authenticity) — SHA-256 is entirely adequate for it. Confirmed as the inventory's record of the store's only hash use. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256 family: A256KW key wrap + A256CBC-HS512 / A256GCM content encryption; accepted in WithContentEncryption (Algorithm.cs:90-91) and supported for keygen (CryptoService.cs:92). Grover leaves a 128-bit margin — the strongest symmetric option this library offers and the CNSA 2.0-compliant size. All 44 sites genuine.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: .NET RandomNumberGenerator.Fill — the OS CSPRNG — in CryptoService.CreateRandomKey, the single randomness source for every key this library generates (RSA, ECDSA, HMAC and AES keys, plus key IDs via CreateUniqueId). Correct and quantum-safe posture control; recorded so the inventory shows keygen randomness is sound (no System.Random or seeded RNG anywhere in the key path). Changeable here.
